headline: React Mastery Series Focuses on Production-Ready App Architecture
summary: Learn how to organize your React applications for scalability and maintainability, focusing on feature-based architecture and best practices for enterprise development.
details: Building real-world React applications requires more than just understanding individual concepts. This series delves into proper architecture to ensure projects remain scalable, maintainable, and easy for teams to collaborate on.

Feature-based architecture is highlighted as the preferred approach for large applications, ensuring that components like a Button remain focused on UI rendering and do not need to know about complex business logic or API communication.

Key principles include organizing applications by features, separating concerns so services handle API communication, utilizing custom hooks for reusable business logic, and ensuring components are primarily responsible for UI rendering.
The adoption of TypeScript is emphasized as a standard requirement for modern React development, further enhancing the robustness and maintainability of enterprise-grade applications.
By implementing clean architecture, developers can significantly improve development speed and overall project maintainability, leading to more efficient and successful software delivery.

headline_marked: [[Ars Notoria]]: Medieval AI promised instant knowledge
headline: Ars Notoria: Medieval AI promised instant knowledge
summary: Centuries before The Matrix, scholars used diagrams and incantations to fast-track learning, but church authorities condemned it as demonic.
details: The Ars Notoria, a medieval manuscript, promised scholars a shortcut to advanced knowledge through diagrams, incantations, and arcane rituals, bypassing years of study.
Unlike other magical texts, its diagrams were not illustrative or models for equipment, but were believed to offer direct contact with supernatural forces, akin to religious icons.
Practitioners recited complex verbal formulae and unintelligible words, imprinted labyrinthine images, and engaged in an act of faith to receive knowledge.
The text presented its rituals as pious prayers and claimed its alien words came from ancient languages, preserving names of angels.
However, theologians like Thomas Aquinas condemned the Ars Notoria as 'unlawful and futile,' warning that its misunderstood signs could lead to demonic contact.
Despite condemnation, the manuscript's survival in numerous copies and continued ownership in religious institutions until the late medieval period show its enduring appeal.
